chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated that Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Zarif ibn Nasih, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon them both)

He said: 'The Shia of Ali are those who sacrifice themselves in our Wilayah, who love one another due to our Mawaddah, who visit one another to revive our affairs. If they get angry, they do not oppress; if they are pleased, they do not exceed bounds. They are a blessing for those who live near them, and a source of peace for those who associate with them.' And I have narrated what I have recorded in this meaning in the book Sifat al-Shia.

key_terms.صِفَاتِ الشِّيعَةِ: Sifat al-Shia (The Characteristics of the Shia, a book by Al-Saduq)

ai.seo_question: What are the defining characteristics of the Shia according to this hadith from al-Khisal?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights these traits as the definitive markers of *al-Shi'a al-Haqq* (the true party of Ali), linking social cohesion (*muwadda*) directly to spiritual fidelity. The description of emotional equilibrium—avoiding oppression in anger and extravagance in joy—reflects the Shia ideal of *i'tidal* (moderation), while the emphasis on neighborly blessing underscores the communal responsibility of the faithful. This passage serves as a practical ethical framework for distinguishing genuine adherents from nominal ones based on their interpersonal conduct.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-104 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Faz’zal, on the authority of Zarif ibn Nasih, on the authority of Amr ibn Abil Miqdam that Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (MGB) said, “

Indeed our followers are those who sacrifice their lives for loving us; become friends with each other due to loving us; visit each other to revive our traditions; do not oppress anyone if they get angry; do not go beyond bounds if they like some thing; do not waste; are blessings for their neighbors; and are a source of peace and comfort for those with whom they associate.”I have explained this in more detail in Sifat ul-Shia.
